# Exact constraints for the tetrahedral scalar-correction candidate

The candidate in this note is NOT proved. The purpose is to state its exact
finite rational inequalities and to record a certified failure of extending
the same formula outside its proposed central domain.

Use the complete quadrilateral parameterization in
`candidate 5c1f3bb21840ea60`. In this note the
positive diagonal coordinates x,y,z,w need not sum to one; set S=x+y+z+w.
Their normalized coordinates are the actual diagonal intersection.

Write

    P=x+y, R=z+w, a=xy, b=zw,
    D=(x+z)(x+w)(y+z)(y+w)
      =(a-b)^2+S(aR+bP),
    F_num=b(PS-a+b),
    s_num=3S(bP-aR).

The cap fraction and scalar moment are F=F_num/D and s=s_num/(4D).
Set

    D_0=(x+z)(x+w), D_1=(y+z)(y+w),
    D_2=(x+z)(y+z), D_3=(x+w)(y+w),
    N_0=x[S(2x+z+w)-D_0],
    N_1=y[S(2y+z+w)-D_1],
    N_2=z[S(x+y+2z)-D_2],
    N_3=w[S(x+y+2w)-D_3].

Then λ_i=N_i/(3S D_i). Every N_i is positive. The central inequalities
λ_i<=1/3 are, respectively,

    b(S+x)-x^2 y>=0,    b(S+y)-xy^2>=0,
    a(S+z)-z^2 w>=0,    a(S+w)-zw^2>=0.                (1)

By the ordering lemma already proved in the diagonal note, one may assume
x<=y and z<=w, with the same within-pair orders for λ. The possible middle
coordinate pairs in the sorted four-tuple λ are therefore

    {0,1}, {2,3}, {1,2}, {0,3}.

For the selected middle pair {j,k}, the explicit correction from the
proved vertex-section theorem is

    c=4/[12-1/λ_j-1/λ_k]
     =4N_jN_k/B_jk,
    B_jk=12N_jN_k-3S(D_jN_k+D_kN_j)>0.                (2)

Positivity is supplied by the central-domain denominator proof in
`candidate 1f9aa6ef8c94292a`; it is not a new assumption.
The conjectured extension to all quadrilateral sections is

    27/64 <= F-cs <=37/64.                             (3)

The lower half of (3) is exactly the homogeneous degree-ten inequality

    (64F_num-27D)B_jk-192S(bP-aR)N_jN_k>=0.            (4)

The upper half is equivalently

    (37D-64F_num)B_jk+192S(bP-aR)N_jN_k>=0.            (5)

The factors cleared in deriving these are all positive on the stated
domain. No rational approximation, limit of centers, or numerical
interpretation occurs in this algebraic reduction.

For example, if the middle pair is {2,3}, its full order constraints may
be taken as x<=y, z<=w, and

    N_2(x+w)-N_0(y+z)>=0,                              (6)
    N_1(x+w)-N_3(y+z)>=0.                              (7)

These are exactly λ_0<=λ_2 and λ_3<=λ_1 after cancellation of positive
common denominator factors. Together with the central inequality for λ_1,
they imply the other central inequalities, although retaining all four
inequalities in (1) is harmless for a positivity certificate.

A computer search for nonnegative polynomial-multiplier certificates in
a restricted cone at degrees 10 through 14 did not find one. This does
not refute (3), and no such certificate is claimed. Sampled exact tests
and constrained numerical extrema are only search evidence and are not
used to infer (4) or (5).

## Exact obstruction outside the central domain

Take normalized diagonal coordinates

    e=(16,29,5,8)/58.

Its section centroid is

    λ=(78/203,715/1887,3095/31059,1325/9657).

The first two coordinates exceed 1/3. Applying the same sorted-middle
formula nevertheless gives the positive number

    c=378950/196347.

The corrected quadrilateral cap fraction is

    F-cs=172480645/247004526 >37/64.

Thus extending this PARTICULAR formula for c outside the central domain
is false. This does not contradict the weighted stationary-section
inequality or the possible existence of some other scalar correction.
Any proof using (3) in the central domain must treat these other centroids
by a separate argument.
